topic: What if Earth suddenly stopped spinning? Everything not fixed down would keep moving east at the speed of Earth's spin, which is about 1,670 km/h at the equator, and a day would last a whole year.

episode.title: What If Earth Suddenly Stopped Spinning?

shots.narration: What if Earth suddenly stopped spinning—but everything else kept moving?
shots.scene: Colourful 3D science lab, vertical frame, glowing Earth hologram between Nova and Byte, no text or symbols.
shots.action: Nova presents a spinning Earth hologram to Byte.
shots.mood: Bright cyan lighting, wide-eyed curiosity, vivid planetary colours.

shots.narration: Imagine Earth's rotation stopping while its journey around the Sun continues.
shots.scene: Vertical lab view with a large Sun and Earth orbital hologram, Earth's continents clearly visible, no text.
shots.action: Nova freezes the holographic Earth's rotation along its continuing orbital path.
shots.mood: Glowing gold sunlight, crisp blue planet, curious scientific wonder.

shots.narration: [surprised] Loose objects keep moving east, carried by their original momentum.
shots.scene: Lab hologram enlarged into an unoccupied equatorial landscape with loose colourful balls above solid ground, no text.
shots.action: The loose balls streak eastward over the stopped landscape.
shots.mood: Bright motion trails, playful demonstration, startling contrast.

shots.narration: At the equator, that's about 1,670 km/h!
shots.scene: Colourful lab with an Earth hologram featuring a luminous equatorial band and a tiny unmarked loose sphere, no text.
shots.action: The loose sphere races eastward along the holographic equator.
shots.mood: Electric blue glow, vivid speed trails, astonished robot eyes.

shots.narration: The atmosphere keeps moving too, creating powerful winds.
shots.scene: Vertical cutaway Earth hologram in the lab, solid continents beneath a translucent atmosphere, no text.
shots.action: Bright atmospheric ribbons sweep eastward over the stationary surface.
shots.mood: Swirling turquoise light, dramatic but clean educational imagery.

shots.narration: [excited] Oceans also surge onward, sweeping across coastlines.
shots.scene: Contained tabletop hologram of blue ocean beside an empty rocky coastline, Nova and Byte behind it, no buildings or text.
shots.action: Holographic ocean water surges over the empty coastline.
shots.mood: Luminous blue water, impressive scale, safe laboratory demonstration.

shots.narration: But Earth would still travel around the Sun.
shots.scene: Colourful lab with a tall solar-system hologram, Earth maintaining a fixed orientation beside a glowing Sun, no text.
shots.action: Nova traces Earth's continuing orbital path with her finger.
shots.mood: Warm gold and deep blue, calm discovery after the motion.

shots.narration: Without spinning, sunlight creeps around Earth as it orbits.
shots.scene: Close vertical view of a nonrotating Earth hologram beside the Sun, Byte hovering at the edge, no text.
shots.action: The daylight boundary gradually crosses Earth's surface during its orbit.
shots.mood: Gentle golden illumination, deep violet night, quiet wonder.

shots.narration: [surprised] One day lasts a year—what if Earth stopped orbiting?
shots.scene: Vertical science lab with a glowing Sun and Earth hologram on a luminous orbital ring, no text.
shots.action: Nova lifts the orbital ring away from the Earth hologram.
shots.mood: Bright golden glow, intrigued expressions, inviting scientific mystery.

episode.endHook: What if Earth stopped orbiting the Sun?
episode.description: Dr. Nova shows Byte why stopping Earth would not stop everything on it. Explore eastward momentum, rushing oceans, and a day that lasts a whole year.
